text: DSH Activity Heat 是面向 Web 客户端的会话热度插件：它根据最近活动时间为会话和工作区计算热度，并把信息呈现在侧边栏会话标题、悬停卡片和独立面板中。面板可切换会话与工作区，按热度筛选并查看最近活跃项目；还提供右侧栏入口、/heat 命令和活跃会话底栏。适合需要快速找回刚处理过的会话或查看当前活跃工作的 DSH 用户。无需 API 密钥或外部账号。

DSH Activity Heat scores sessions and workspaces by recent activity, showing heat in sidebar titles, hover cards, and a panel. Switch views, filter by heat, or open it with the /heat command. A bottom bar highlights active sessions. No API key or external account is required.
想快速找到刚才聊过的 DSH 会话。
能不能按最近活跃程度浏览会话和工作区？
DSH Activity Heat 的功能「会话热度面板」：按最近活动和运行状态计算热度，支持会话与工作区视图及热度筛选；可从侧栏或 /heat 打开。
DSH Activity Heat 的功能「侧栏热度提示」：在会话标题和悬停卡片显示热度等级，并将运行中的会话优先排序。
DSH Activity Heat 的功能「侧栏热度提示」：在会话标题前显示热度点，并在悬停卡片中呈现热度等级；会话运行状态也会影响热度排序。用户浏览侧栏会话时即可查看。

@local/activity-heat README · Why：Sessions pile up in the DSH sidebar, nested inside workspace groups. The one you just spoke in is pushed out of sight within minutes.

This plugin computes a 0–100% heat score from **time since last activity** and expresses it in three places plus a panel — the more recent, the more visible.

@local/activity-heat README · What you see：| Where | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Sidebar entry** | A heat-ring icon whose brightness follows the hottest session in the profile |
| **Session title** | A small dot before the title text: solid = warm/blazing, hollow = active and cooler. Cold sessions are grey, hotter ones turn blue; active sessions pulse gently; hidden after 7 days. The row-leading cell stays with the host's state dot and the schedule clock |
| **Session hover card** | `Heat 4/5 · Warm`, `Last active: 40 min ago`, `This workspace is hot`; the status line is rendered natively by the host (Running / Waiting for approval / Plan review / Waiting for answer / Completed / Idle) |
| **Main panel** | Sessions / Workspaces views, each with heat filters and a count selector |

@local/activity-heat README · Panel：- **Top-level switch**: `Sessions 58` / `Workspaces 10` — no more mixed list
- **Two-row toolbar, one material**: the panel draws no title. The **primary row** holds the Sessions/Workspaces switch, the range switch (Active / Archived / Subagents), and a right-aligned count picker labelled *Count* with Select. The **filter row** is its own line: heat bands as pill chips with a count badge, horizontally scrollable. Every control shares **one glass surface** (translucent fill + hairline border + top highlight); the active state only layers blue fill/border/text on that same glass, so hierarchy comes from accent strength alone — never a mix of solid white blocks, bare text and solid blue pills.
- **Count selector**: sessions `10 / 20 / 30 / 50`, workspaces `5 / 10 / 20`
- **Heat filter**: All / Blazing / Warm / Active / Recent / Stale, with live counts
- **Every card**: the bottom row is split into three groups divided by hairlines — ① cache hit rate + context usage (each with a mini progress bar) ② turns + steps + tokens ③ accumulated conversation time; items inside a group use a dot, groups are separated by a vertical rule. @local/activity-heat README · Right-click menu：| Action | Notes |
|---|---|
| Open session | Same as clicking the card |
| Open in terminal | Opens the session/workspace directory in the system terminal: Windows tries Windows Terminal → PowerShell 7 → Windows PowerShell; macOS uses Terminal; Linux uses x-terminal-emulator |
| Open in… | Two-level cascading menu (hover submenu in the panel; the native sidebar row menu expands the same submenu on hover — no second click). The first row is always "Open in terminal"; the rest list locally probed file managers / editors / terminals (including Git Bash and WSL); picking one opens the session/workspace directory there |
| Copy session ID / title / latest prompt / working directory | The latest prompt is copied in full; clipboard failures are reported |
| Pin / unpin | Writes the host sidebar order; this panel keeps sorting by heat |
| Rename… | Prefilled with the current title; an empty title cannot be saved |
| Fork session | Creates a branch at the last completed turn without navigating |
| Download session log | Uses the host `api/session.export` route; reports unavailability when the export package is not mounted |
| Archive session |

@local/activity-heat README · Right-click menu：Workspace cards also offer open workspace, open in…, new session in workspace, and copy workspace name / path. Ungrouped cards have no actionable entries and ignore right-click.

The menu is portaled to `document.body` so the scrolling list cannot clip it; arrow keys plus Enter cover every action, `Esc` or an outside click closes it, and focus returns to the card.
@local/activity-heat README · Session status (native-aligned)：Status model, labels and colours all follow the host's `sessionStatuses()`; the plugin no longer draws its own whale-tail status marks:

@local/activity-heat README · Session status (native-aligned)：- **Running**: `running === true`, blue `StateDot` spinner + "Running"; the card gets the orbiting band and breathing glow, and DeepSeek whales swim back and forth along the bottom edge (one more every minute, up to 5).
- **Waiting for approval / Plan awaiting review / Waiting for answer**: `pendingInteraction.kind` is approval / plan-review / question, amber warning dot; highest priority.
- **Completed**: `completionUnread === true` (a non-main session finished but unread), green dot + "Completed"; clears when opened.
- **Idle**: anything else; no dot in the row, grey dot in detail views.
- **Additive**: when `runningSubagentCount > 0`, "N subagents running" is shown alongside the primary state.
- **Data source**: prefer the `useSessionStatus` snapshot; only fall back to `summary.running`, `userQuestions.active` or the local seen watermark when that snapshot is missing. Running sessions still count as heat 5/5 and sort first.
- **Row-leading cell stays with the host**: the native state dot and schedule clock live there; the plugin puts nothing in it and shows heat only as the small dot before the title.

@local/activity-heat README · Session status (native-aligned)：**Workspace cards**: when any session inside the workspace is Running, the card shows the same running frame and "Running" mark, so live work is visible from the Workspaces view too.

@local/activity-heat README · Session status (native-aligned)：A workspace card also aggregates everything that can be summed: session count, turns, steps, tokens and total conversation time. Cache hit rate is weighted across the workspace's billing buckets (not an average of percentages), and context usage shows the most loaded session. Nothing that cannot be summarised — prompts, the current-session flag — is carried over.

> `prefers-reduced-motion` is respected: with reduced motion enabled, all animation stops.

@local/activity-heat README · New in 0.4–0.5 — more than one panel：- **Native-aligned session status**: Waiting for approval / Plan awaiting review / Waiting for answer / Running / Completed / Idle, drawn with a local `StatusDot` that mirrors the host’s, from `useSessionStatus`; subagents stack on top of the primary state.
- **Range views**: the session view switches between Active / Archived / Subagents; archived rows can be restored in place.
- **Lightweight entries**: the sidebar “More” menu and the `/heat` command — reach the panel without opening it (the collapsed badge is no longer registered because the host uses that seam for its update badge). The session-header corner seat belongs to ui-sidebar-right’s panel button, so this plugin no longer contends for it.
- **Bottom active-sessions bar (full-width page bottom)**: mounted on `shell.bottom` (the full-width row below all three columns); appears only when sessions are running or waiting, click to open; nothing reserved when idle. **Do not mount it on `conversation.composer.dock`** — the host’s own session stats (turns/steps/speed, tokens/cache hit) live there and would collide with the stats row.
- **Batch actions**: Select

@local/activity-heat README · Look and motion：Every surface is built from host theme tokens plus `color-mix` — **no hard-coded colors** — so light and dark themes work automatically:

```css
--color-blue-500             /* heat color (blue, falls back to #3b82f6) */
--dsw-alias-bg-base          /* opaque card background (hides the orbit band) */
--dsw-specific-menu          /* glass surface: host translucent menu fill (light #f8f9fa94 / dark #43454a73) */
--dsw-menu-backdrop-filter   /* background blur: blur(40px) saturate(150%) */

@local/activity-heat README · Look and motion：Heat uses just **three bands — light grey → deep grey → bright blue** (`HEAT_TONES`): light grey for cold/stale/recent, deep grey for active, bright blue for warm/blazing. The bar **keeps its band colour for the full height** and only brightens toward the top (the same tone mixed with white, `heatBarSurface`), with a 1px inner highlight and a hairline glass edge (`heatBarShadow`) — so it reads as a lit glass rod, and the lower half no longer dissolves into the card. The grey steps use the neutral `label` tokens, which read as light grey in light themes and dark grey in dark themes — no per-theme colours.

@local/activity-heat README · Look and motion：Heat meters and heat bars are **continuous, tick-free fills** shaped like “water rushing against a baffle in a pipe”: the track and water body are shaded as a **cylindrical section** (darker top/bottom, brighter middle), the fill is the tier colour with a liquid-level gradient that gently sloshes, caustics drift forward around the upper-middle of the bore while a water-surface glint rises and falls slightly above centre, and the leading edge is a bright water wall inset top and bottom, centred, with a soft surge and periodic ripple. Warm tiers add a matching glow; every heat-bar surface shares the same styling.

@local/activity-heat README · Look and motion：The **left edge of each card is a workspace bookmark rail** (`ah-ws-tag`): a full-height, lightly tinted left column with an 11px folder icon and the workspace name (`.82em`, **single-line ellipsis**, full name on hover), icon aligned with the name and content horizontally centered, separated from the body by a hairline vertical rule; **the session status is responsive (in a right-side status column at ≥960px, or below the name when narrower)**; width `clamp(104px,16%,196px)`; when there is no workspace the same-width rail is kept. The vertical thermometer is removed; workspace-view cards already show the name as their title.

@local/activity-heat README · Look and motion：- **Transitions** — the list fades in when the view, filter or count changes, with a `min(index, 8) × 20 ms` stagger; filter chips cross-fade their fill and border; segmented controls cross-fade their fill.
- **Hover** — cards lift 1px with a soft outer glow while the frosted layer fades in; pressing settles them back. Meta chips get a tinted capsule, and heat bars/meters glow a little brighter. There is **no one-shot sheen**; the heat bar itself is a continuous forward water current (the only looping effect).
- **Hover cards** — 170 ms pop-in and a 130 ms reverse pop-out (the direction follows the up/down flip); the timing donut rotates into place and the timeline segments grow in sequence.
- **Sidebar** — the title dot is a radial gradient with a soft glow and grows a 3px halo when its row is hovered; the entry ring uses a `conic-gradient` and brightens on hover.

@local/activity-heat README · Look and motion：Performance trade-off: static cards never run `backdrop-filter` (a 50-row list stays smooth) — only the hovered card and the popover are truly frosted. The list fades at its edges with gradient masks instead of `mask`, so the frosted children are not broken.
@local/activity-heat README · Install：This plugin is installed as a local directory or a GitHub repository; it is **not published to npm** (`private: true`).
@local/activity-heat README · Option 1 — GitHub (recommended)：```bash

@local/activity-heat README · inside your DSH profile directory：cd ~/.dsh/profiles/<your-profile>
pnpm add github:MarkTina/dsh-activity-heat#v0.5.3
```

Pin a tag (`#v0.5.3`) rather than following `main`, so an unrelated commit cannot change what you run. To upgrade later, bump the tag and restart DSH.

The repository must be **public**; a private repo needs a token (`https://<token>@github.com/...` or an SSH remote) before `pnpm add` can fetch it.json
"@local/activity-heat"
```

@local/activity-heat README · inside your DSH profile directory：**First install** normally activates through the host's HMR — if the row does not appear, restart DSH once. **Updating an already-installed copy** (same path, changed files) always needs a full quit-and-relaunch: a page refresh only reloads the UI, and toggling the plugin does not re-read changed modules.

@local/activity-heat README · inside your DSH profile directory：> Desktop profiles are managed by the Electron app. Install through its plugin manager (GitHub / local directory) rather than running `pnpm` inside `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop` — the app owns that directory and will reject or overwrite manual changes.

@local/activity-heat README · Option 2 — Local checkout：```bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/<your-profile>
pnpm add link:/absolute/path/dsh-activity-heat
```

Add `@local/activity-heat` to `dsh.profile.bundles` the same way.

@local/activity-heat README · Shortcut：> **Why not `Ctrl+H`?** The host treats `Ctrl` + `C/V/X/Z/Y/Q/H` as reserved system keys (browser history etc.), so a bare `Ctrl+H` default is rejected as `reserved`. Adding `alt` uses the web whitelist branch. For the same reason the plugin deliberately declares **no Linux profile** — on Linux `alt+control` is treated as reserved and would fail the whole registration. Linux users can bind a key in Settings.

@local/activity-heat README · Configuration：Defaults live in `cordis.patch.yml`. To override, add a row with the same id to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (**config is replaced whole, not deep-merged — write every field**):

```yaml
- id: activity-heat
  config:
    hotMinutes: 10        # blazing window (minutes)
    warmMinutes: 60       # warm
@local/activity-heat README · Data sources：Everything is read from **public host snapshots** — no private APIs, nothing written to the session log:

@local/activity-heat README · Data sources：| Purpose | Source |
|---|---|
| Last activity time | `sessions.list.byId[id].updatedAt` (same as the sidebar row trailing time) |
| Title / draft / subagent / archive | the same `title` `blank` `origin`, plus `workspaces.list.archivedSessionIds` |
| Workspace membership | `workspaces.list.items[].sessionIds` (same mapping as the host `groupByWorkspace`) |
| Turns / steps | `sessions.list.projectionsBySession[id].values.sessionStats.turns` / `.steps` — the values the composer activity pill reads |
| Tokens | `…values.tokenUsage` — billed input (`uncachedInputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheWriteTokens`) plus `outputTokens`, the same whole-log total as the composer usage pill |
| Cache hit rate | `…values.tokenUsage.cacheReadTokens / billed input`, using the host's own rounding (a partial hit never displays as 100%) |
| Context usage | `…values.contextPressure` — `projectedTokens ?? pressureTokens` over `contextWindow`, the value the composer context meter reads |
| Session prompt | `…values.contextTimeline` (`initialPrompt` / `lastUser` / `lastReply`) — the status bar does not show prompts |
| Conversation time & breakdown | `…values.conte
@local/activity-heat README · Data sources：**Excluded**: archived sessions, subagent child sessions, blank draft sessions.

@local/activity-heat README · Repository layout：The package follows the DSH bundle layout: a Host entry, a Web client entry, one loader patch, and exported display resources.

```
dsh-activity-heat/
├── index.js            Host half — open-terminal route (launches the system terminal); otherwise mount-only
├── client.js           Web half — ModuleLoader factory, slots, locale
├── DESIGN.md           Design charter — red lines; deviations in VETO-LIST.md

@local/activity-heat README · Repository layout：Visible UI text is routed through the host **Client locale service** (`ctx.locale`), falling back to the bundled Chinese dictionary when the service is unavailable. The two locale JSON files carry the same keys; `node test/locale.cjs` keeps them and the inlined dictionary in sync.

@local/activity-heat README · Debugging：Release builds log nothing. To trace the full chain, flip the switch at the top of `client.js` to `true` and reload the page:

```js
var ACTIVITY_HEAT_DEBUG = false;   // ← change to true
```

@local/activity-heat README · Self-checks：The repo ships dependency-free logic tests that load the **real `client.js`** against a minimal React stand-in — no browser required:

```bash
node test/panel.cjs        # registration / sorting / filtering / rendering / click-through
node test/menu.cjs         # right-click menu: actions, confirmation, export probe, capability fallback
node test/shortcut.cjs     # shortcut defaults against host reserved-key rules
node test/boot-timing.cjs  # restart timing: recovery when slots become ready late
@local/activity-heat README · Self-checks：`pnpm test` runs all five.

@local/activity-heat README · Known limitations：- Turns, tokens, cache hit rate and context usage read `sessionStats`, `tokenUsage` and `contextPressure` — the same projections as the composer status bar, so the numbers match it exactly. Profiles that only expose `contextTimeline` fall back to its values; in that case the figures can differ from the status bar.
- No Linux default shortcut is declared; Linux users bind one in Settings.
- The right-click menu does **not** delete sessions: the host only supports archiving, and archived sessions can be restored from the sidebar's archived view.
- Running sessions' archive item becomes “Stop and archive…”: the dialog lists the running turn / subagents / jobs / schedules and stops them (irreversible) before archiving; the panel re-sorts by heat afterwards.
- "Download session log" requires the host to mount `dsh-session-log-export`; without it the item reports unavailability instead of opening a 404 page.
- The host's native sidebar rows expose no right-click event, but they do expose `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` / `.row.action` seats; the plugin's terminal / copy / download actions live there, while pin / rename / fork / archi
